2017_113_boardbook091917.paragraph: Board book for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of September 19, 2017 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. It carries the July 2017 Treasurer's Report, with total disbursements in period of $5,084,291.90 and a General Fund balance of $22,363,673 at July 31, 2017; nineteen new teacher hires with biographical sketches; a staffing report counting 46 new teachers; the September enrollment comparison showing 13,016 students against 12,817 a year earlier; and the award of BID 9844 for weight room equipment at Athens and Troy High Schools to All-Pro Exercise at $80,138.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, September 19, 2017, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098.

**Recognition**
Dr. Erin Detmer is welcomed as principal of Leonard Elementary, appointed at the July 18th meeting; she holds a B.S. in Elementary Education from Central Michigan, a Masters in Reading & Language Arts and a Ph.D. in Reading from Oakland University, and served as Literacy Specialist and Head Teacher at Hill Elementary. Mr. Jolly reads biographies of the eleven Spring 2017 All-State Athletes. Mark Dziatczak, Kris Griffor and Jennifer Gottlieb present a Mission Moment on Camp oneTROY. ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2016, recognizing Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services. The Michigan Association of School Boards' Honor Board achievement and Standard of Excellence Award are presented to the Board, and President Nancy Philippart receives the MASB Master Platinum Award, which requires a minimum of 813 education credits. Four student representatives are introduced: Anjana Pisupati (IA-East), Nadia Shaouni (Troy College & Career), Tori Zarbaugh (Athens) and Hana Barre (Troy High).

**Treasurer's Report — July 2017**
Rick West certifies the disbursements. Check disbursements total $2,850,062.11 — General Fund $2,731,045.57, Special Revenue Funds $48,915.74, Other Funds $70,100.80 — with ACH debits of $14,691.66, outgoing wire transfers of $2,151,276.75, P-Card purchases of $73,305.13 and prior period void disbursements of ($5,043.75), for total disbursements in period of $5,084,291.90.

In the General Fund, total expenditures are budgeted at $147,430,144 against $1,813,012 spent and $93,099,272 encumbered, leaving $52,517,860 available, 35.62 percent. Total instruction is budgeted at $101,335,630 and total support services at $45,952,718. Capital Projects budgets $21,615,000 of capital outlay and $4,105,000 in proceeds from the sale of land.

**Personnel**
Nineteen probationary teaching contracts are recommended for 2017-2018, each with a biographical sketch: Margaret Burchi (.8 Resource Room, Larson), Sarah Misch (4th Grade, Wattles), Kimberly Mitchell (Resource Room, Athens), Justine Galbraith (Spanish/English, Boulan Park), Shannon Dziwanowski (.6 Science, Larson/Boulan Park), Crissy Karaszewski (Counselor, Boulan Park), Jessica Buckley (Resource Room, Leonard), Spencer Mossoian (Psychologist, Services), Sarah Kijek (2nd Grade, Hill), Kaleigh Roberts (4th Grade, Leonard), Amanda Oppenlander (4th Grade, Costello), Alexandra Biggert (1st Grade, Barnard), Maura Donovan (Kindergarten, Bemis), Kathryn Berry (Music, Bemis), Lyndsey Versteegden (5th Grade, Morse), Lindsay Kuroski (Social Worker, Services), Allison Patterson (Spanish), Paul Sandy (.4 Social Studies, Larson) and Lisa Knudson (English, Troy High). Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reports 46 new TSD teachers, of whom 3 are TSD graduates, 24 hold education beyond a Bachelor's Degree, and 18 have five or more years of previous teaching experience (9 of those with ten or more years), bringing 204 total years of previous teaching experience as a group.

**Curriculum**
Mark Dziatczak presents the 2017 summer professional learning summary under the district's "World Class by 2020" vision, covering the NGSX Science Workshop, technology integration, summer curriculum development, New Pedagogies for Deep Learning, administrative visioning, secondary math flexible learning spaces, Camp OneTroy, Reading Recovery development, the TSD Literacy Project, new teacher orientation, and welcome-back professional learning with George Couros. Dziatczak and Kris Griffor then give the enrollment update: 13,016 total students on September 19, 2017 against 12,817 on September 20, 2016, with elementary at 5630 (from 5,542), middle schools at 2994 (from 2,988) and the high school group at 4392 (from 4,287).

**Business and Other**
BID 9844, weight room equipment for Athens and Troy High Schools, drew six responses from eight invited bidders; Todd Hensley and Mike Jolly recommend All-Pro Exercise as the lowest qualified bidder to specifications at $80,138.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. The Board certifies Steve Gottlieb, Gary Hauff and Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2017 Delegate Assembly, November 9-12, 2017, and Dr. Machesky reports on oneTROY for 2017/2018 with the video from the August 29th staff Welcome Back event.

Board book for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, September 19, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda runs: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (A-F); Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General – Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment.

**Recognition.** 2.A welcomes Dr. Erin Detmer as the new principal of Leonard Elementary School, appointed at the July 18th Board meeting; she and the Leonard staff were not present in July because of summer vacation. Detmer holds a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education from Central Michigan, a Masters in Reading & Language Arts and a Ph.D. in Reading from Oakland University, and served as Literacy Specialist and Head Teacher at Hill Elementary for two years, having taught second grade at both Hill and Leonard before that.

2.B recognizes the All-State Athletes for Spring 2017, with Mr. Jolly reading biographies: Max Cavellier (Senior, Athens, Boys Lacrosse), Lauren Fulcher (Sophomore, Troy High, Track), Grace Johnson (Freshman, Troy High, Track), Kyle Kohl (Senior, Athens, Boys Lacrosse), Allison Leonard (Freshman, Athens, Girls Soccer), Ashley Leonard (Senior, Athens, Girls Soccer), Jacob Lining (Senior, Athens, Boys Lacrosse), Morgan MacDonald (Sophomore, Troy High, Girls Lacrosse), Justin Parry (Senior, Troy High, Boys Lacrosse), Connor Wilson (Senior, Troy High, Baseball) and Megan Worrel (Junior, Troy High, Track).

2.C is a TSD Mission Moment on Camp oneTROY, presented by Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent for Elementary Instruction, and Jennifer Gottlieb, Director of Student Growth, Equity and Accountability.

2.D presents the Association of School Business Officials International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting, honoring the district for its Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2016, and recognizing Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and his staff. The certificate is signed by Anthony N. Dragona, Ed.D., RSBA, President, and John D. Musso, CAE, Executive Director. A September 14, 2017 letter from Musso to West notes that the Certificate of Excellence Review Team provided comments for improvement that must be addressed and included, with the district's written responses, in next year's application packet. The attached press release, issued from Reston, VA with Susan Lambert of ASBO International as contact (slambert@asbointl.org, 866.682.2729 x7067), describes the award as sponsored by VALIC, a division of AIG that as of December 31, 2015 had more than $83 billion in total assets under management and managed plans for nearly 24,000 groups serving more than 2 million participants; AIG serves customers in more than 100 countries and jurisdictions. ASBO International, founded in 1910, is a professional organization of 5,000 members.

2.E presents the Michigan Association of School Boards' Honor Board achievement and Standard of Excellence Award, both awarded the previous June, and honors Board President Nancy Philippart for the MASB Master Platinum Award, which requires a minimum of 813 education credits. The item notes the Troy community has seven Board members committed to life-long learning and positive policy making.

2.F introduces the student representatives to the Board. Anjana Pisupati is a junior at IA-East, a student council officer active in HOSA, Model United Nations and the Indian-American Student Association, who would like to pursue business. Nadia Shaouni is a senior at Troy College & Career High School enrolled since November of the prior year, meeting her credit requirements in January, planning two years at Oakland Community College before transferring to Wayne State University for a degree in Psychology; she describes struggling with a learning and comprehension disability since fourth grade until arriving at TCCHS and praises the one-on-one and emotional support from teachers there. Tori Zarbaugh is a senior at Athens High School, a Summa Cum Laude, Advanced Placement and National Honor Society scholar and co-president of the Athens Theatre Company. Hana Barre is a senior at Troy High School on the Forensics Team, the Social Justice Project and the morning announcements crew.

**Consent agenda.** Item 5 covers minutes of the August 15, 2017 Special Board Workshop, minutes of the August 15, 2017 Board Meeting, and the Treasurer's Report for July 2017.

The August 15 workshop minutes record President Philippart calling the workshop to order at 5:33 p.m. at the Administration Building, with Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Gottlieb, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti and Mr. Schmidt present and Mrs. Hammond participating remotely via Skype; also present were Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Griffor, Pass, Soggs and West, and two members of the audience. The agenda covered public communication, board discussion priorities for 2017-18, and other business; the meeting adjourned at 7:25 p.m. Paula Fleming signed as Secretary.

The August 15 meeting minutes record Philippart calling the meeting to order at 7:37 p.m., with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff, Miletti and Schmidt present, Hammond absent, and the same administrators and two audience members. Resolution 17-075 approved the July 18, 2017 special workshop minutes, the July 18, 2017 meeting minutes and the Treasurer's Report for June 2017. Resolution 17-076 approved new hires: Tyler Hancsak, Gregory Pitman, Joseph Richards, Emily Allen, Justin Herrick, Rachelle Hanson, Sharrisse Thomas, Jessica Suvak, Julia Schwarz, Stephanie Fragomeni, Colleen Bache, Grace Lynch, Christine Bonnell, Colleen Patterson, Amanda Ricketts, Suria Ali-Ahmed, Judith Meininger, Christine Foren, Kathleen Rainey, Alex Keesling, Nancy Robertson, Kristara McAlpine, Stephan Henning, Steve Laudicina, Kathleen Drinkard, Paul Couretas and Abbie Stys. Resolution 17-077, under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, authorized accepting applications for a Schools of Choice program for the 2018-2019 school year for 90 non-resident 9th grade students residing outside Oakland County, where that intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the International Academy East program. Resolution 17-078 awarded the video surveillance software upgrade to Tyco SimplexGrinnell in the amount of $44,682.00 as an expenditure of the General Fund; Mr. Gottlieb asked about the software, monitoring locations and viewing access, and Ms. Soggs stated the software is end of life and will no longer be supported, with discussion of adding more security cameras in all schools and Dr. Machesky noting the District can look at that especially if the sinking fund is supported. Each vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Hammond. In board comments, Mr. Miletti asked when the stadium sound systems would be in and Mr. West indicated likely October; Mr. Gottlieb reported positive feedback on Camp oneTROY and on the recent MASB conference; Dr. Philippart asked about course quality, prompting discussion of consistency in classes and instructors; Mr. Schmidt announced that Karen Wonsowicz of Troy Youth Assistance is retiring; Mr. Hauff commented on the MASB conference; Dr. Machesky announced that IA-East started school that day and thanked Mark Dziatczak, Kris Griffor and Jennifer Gottlieb for Camp oneTROY. The meeting adjourned at 8:28 p.m.

**Treasurer's Report, July 2017.** Rick West transmits the check register including current period voids, ACH debits, wire transfers and P-Card purchases, certifying that the disbursements were payments for district obligations and that materials or services were received or performed. Totals are General Fund $2,731,045.57, Special Revenue Funds $48,915.74 and Other Funds $70,100.80, giving total check disbursements of $2,850,062.11; with ACH debits $14,691.66, outgoing wire transfers $2,151,276.75, P-Card purchases $73,305.13 and prior period void disbursements ($5,043.75), total disbursements in period are $5,084,291.90.

July wire transfers total $2,151,276.75, the largest being W0725801 payroll taxes for 7/14/17 at $878,229.95 and W0804806 payroll taxes for 7/28/17 at $672,085.13, with payroll TSA transfers of $245,947.54, $148,611.11 and $140,213.29, payroll HSA of $39,969.59, payroll MESP of $3,040.00 and $2,990.00, several general fund transfers to NGE, and $571.43 transferred from the General Fund to the Troy Career Center for June WIOA. ACH debits total $14,691.66, comprising Consumers Energy charges of $4,062.31, $16.41 and $9.53 and DTE Energy charges of $10,531.08 and $72.33. P-Card purchases total $73,305.13.

**Personnel.** Item 6.A recommends probationary contracts for the 2017-2018 school year for Margaret Burchi (.8 Resource Room, Larson Middle School), Sarah Misch (1.0 Fourth Grade, Wattles Elementary), Kimberly Mitchell (1.0 Resource Room, Athens High School), Justine Galbraith (1.0 Spanish/English, Boulan Park), Shannon Dziwanowski (.6 Science, Larson/Boulan Park), Crissy Karaszewski (1.0 Counselor, Boulan Park Middle School), Jessica Buckley (1.0 Resource Room, Leonard Elementary), Spencer Mossoian (1.0 Psychologist, Services), Sarah Kijek (1.0 Second Grade, Hill Elementary), Kaleigh Roberts (1.0 Fourth Grade, Leonard Elementary), Amanda Oppenlander (1.0 Fourth Grade, Costello Elementary), Alexandra Biggert (1.0 First Grade, Barnard Elementary), Maura Donovan (1.0 Kindergarten, Bemis Elementary), Kathryn Berry (1.0 Music, Bemis Elementary), Lyndsey Versteegden (1.0 Fifth Grade, Morse Elementary), Lindsay Kuroski (1.0 Social Worker, Services), Allison Patterson (1.0 Spanish), Paul Sandy (.4 Social Studies, Larson Middle School) and Lisa Knudson (1.0 English, Troy High School). Biographical sketches list each hire's degrees, certification dates, prior teaching experience and resident community — among them Wayne State, Oakland University, Michigan State, Hillsdale College, the University of Michigan, Central Michigan, DePaul, the University of Toledo and Western Michigan.

Item 6.B is a staffing update from Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, covering the selection process and welcoming the 2017-2018 cohort. It counts 46 new TSD teachers, of whom 3 are TSD graduates and 24 have educational experience beyond a Bachelor's Degree, with 18 teachers bringing five or more years of previous teaching experience — 9 of those with ten or more years — and 204 total years of previous teaching experience as a group.

**Curriculum.** Item 7.A is Mark Dziatczak's presentation on 2017 summer professional learning, prepared with Kris Griffor and Jennifer Gottlieb under the vision "World Class by 2020" and the OneTroy core values. The summer learning slate comprised the NGSX Science Workshop, technology integration (podcasting, advanced Schoology, See Saw, Shadow Puppet, blogging, digital portfolios, iBook Creator and Adobe Spark), summer curriculum development, New Pedagogies for Deep Learning and the 6 Cs, administrative visioning, secondary math flexible learning spaces, Camp OneTroy, Reading Recovery development, the TSD Literacy Project (Pre-K literacy, Troy Institutes and Teachers College Institutes), new teacher orientation, and welcome-back professional learning with George Couros on "New & Better."

Item 7.B is the enrollment update from Dziatczak and Griffor, comparing September 20, 2016 with September 19, 2017. Elementary schools: Barnard 488 then 502; Bemis 521 then 553; Costello 359 then 362; Hamilton 509 then 518; Hill 324 then 334; Leonard 435 then 422; Martell 503 then 489; Morse 464 then 501; Schroeder 514 then 519; Troy Union 472 then 467; Wass 426 then 425; Wattles 492 then 500; Early Childhood Niles 35 then 38; elementary total 5,542 then 5630. Middle schools: Baker 736 then 712; Boulan Park 828 then 823; Larson 726 then 784; Smith 698 then 675; total 2,988 then 2994. High schools: Athens 1,578 then 1562; Troy 1,983 then 2054; IAE 556 then 582; Troy College & Career High School 103 then 126; Troy Center for Transition/Search 67 then 68; total 4,287 then 4392. Total students: 12,817 then 13,016.

**Business.** Item 8.A considers weight room equipment for Athens and Troy High Schools. Invitations were sent to eight potential bidders for closed sealed pricing and six responses were received; the bids were reviewed by Todd Hensley, Purchasing Supervisor, and Mike Jolly, Director of Athletics and Enrichment. The suggested resolution awards the bid to All-Pro Exercise in the amount of $80,138.00 as an expenditure of the 2016 Capital Projects Fund. Hensley's August 30, 2017 memorandum to Rick West, from the Purchasing Department at 1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48093 (phone 248 823-4091, fax 248 823-4013, copied to Pat Orczykowski), recommends All-Pro Exercise as the lowest qualified bidder to specifications for BID 9844. The bid tabulation dated 9/14/2017 shows, by Athens total, Troy total and grand total: All-Pro Exercise $60,825.00, $19,313.00, $80,138.00, with alternates and additional packages bid; Direct Fitness Solutions $70,215.00, $19,675.00, $89,890.00, with an alternate bid; Forte Fitness $61,980.00, $18,365.00, $80,345.00; Exercise Warehouse $66,100.00, $18,550.00, $84,650.00; Matrix $49,454.45, $19,450.01, $68,904.46, marked not to specification; and Pro Maxima $60,842.00, $19,794.00, $80,636.00.

**Other.** Item 10.A certifies Steve Gottlieb, Gary Hauff and Karl Schmidt as the Troy Board of Education's delegates to the Michigan Association of School Boards' 2017 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, November 9-12, 2017; certification allows them to make motions and vote, and the certification is signed by Paula Fleming, Secretary. Item 10.B is Dr. Machesky's report on oneTROY for the 2017/2018 school year, sharing the video created for the Welcome Back Event for all TSD staff at Athens High School on August 29th.
